authoredFrom: M60 ONTOLOGY PASS 2, 2026-10-03. Every shape in the .sql was transcribed from a case the adversarial probe measured on the corpus, and the instrument is committed beside it: `validation/m14/fixtures/sql/adversarial-probe.mts`. Provenance per section: (1) the CTE self-reference is the shape of duckdb/benchmark/recursive_cte/queries/performance/asql_cyk_using_key.sql, where `uses global->parse` was published for the recursive CTE's own name; (2) the qualified call and qualified table reference are the ordinary shapes the probe counted on 5 and 7 files respectively — `processCalls` and `processTrigger` passed no metadata, so `evidenceClassFor`'s `reference_qualified` tier was unreachable for `calls`, and `evidenceClassFor`'s `Uses` arm hardcoded `usage_contextual` while `addTableEdge` had always passed `qualified`; (3) the index-before-table order is what a migration that adds an index before the table writes, and 70 containment edges in a 200-file corpus slice had a member symbol with `ownerName: undefined`; (4) the function-then-view pair is the shape of hasura-engine/server/src-rsr/migrations/10_to_11.sql lines 7 and 25, where `state.redeclared` keyed on the name alone counted two different objects sharing a name as one redefinition — the corpus construct probe measured 15 same-kind OR REPLACE redeclarations against the analyzer's 22 emitted `overrides` edges, and the 7-edge gap was this. Pass 2 also fixed the THIRD entry point to the same wrong output, found after the first two were fixed: a WITH list whose `cte` nodes are SIBLINGS under an ERROR node instead of children of a `statement` (duckdb/benchmark/aoc24/queries/day05.sql, 34 unparseable regions in 1,428 lines), where the outermost-statement anchor finds nothing and the whole scope comes back empty.
comment: This fixture exists because the six questions fail INDEPENDENTLY and pass 1 answered only 'does it fire'. Four of the five sections are forbid-side, because each defect is a place where the obvious implementation publishes something that reads true: a CTE's own name as a table, an unqualified `usage_contextual` tier on a reference that names its own schema, a containment edge whose member does not name its owner, and an override between two objects that merely share a name. Section 5 pins the POSITIVE form of the owner adoption — an index declared before its table, which the 200-file slice showed is the case the immediate lookup cannot see — because a fixture that only forbids would also pass if the analyzer emitted nothing at all. The three `forbidSymbols` rows are the CTE names: a CTE alias is a local binding and this analyzer does not publish it as a symbol, which is a stronger statement than the `uses`-edge forbid and is asserted alongside it because the two defects shared a root cause.
